newsitem.title: NORWAY: SOCCER-FIRST-LEG DRAW TIPS BALANCED TIE LIVERPOOL'S WAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIRST-LEG DRAW TIPS BALANCED TIE LIVERPOOL'S WAY.

text.p: Norwegian part-timers Brann Bergen held England's Liverpool to a 1-1 draw in the first leg of their European Cup Winners Cup quarter final on Thursday with Liverpool now favourites to go through in their home leg in two weeks time.

Striker Robbie Fowler's return to scoring form after missing a host of chances in his last two matches was one of the few consolations for Liverpool manager Roy Evans on a night when his team showed inconsistency and made far too many mistakes. But he will be pleased Liverpool came away with a draw from a tricky encounter.

England striker Fowler scored a gem in the ninth minute -- his fourth goal in his last seven games -- running onto a long Neil Ruddock pass, audaciously flicking the ball over defender Per Ove Ludvigsen and volleying ferocme.
But Liverpool's hopes of a goal feast were quickly spoiled as the Norwegians clawed their way back into the match against a defence sorely missing the commanding presence of injured Mark Wright.

Shortly into the second half Brann striker Geir Hasund was quicker to the ball than the Liverpool defenders and scored from the edge of the box with a shot that went in after hitting goalkeeper David James' left-hand post.

Sensing English insecurity, the Norwegians pressed and James pulled off two stunning saves from bustling striker Tore Andre Flo to make Liverpool cautious favourites for the return leg at Anfield in two weeks' time.
